items.title: Waymo says Singapore will be its next international robotaxi city
items.topic: Waymo says Singapore will be its next international robotaxi city
items.summary: Waymo, a leading autonomous vehicle company, has announced that Singapore will be its next international city for robotaxi deployment. This expansion marks Waymo's commitment to globalizing its self-driving technology and services, potentially increasing the availability of autonomous ride-hailing in urban areas.

items.topic: Tesla’s record month: 4 fatal Autopilot and Full Self-Driving crashes

items.topic: We don’t need AI regulation — leave safety to us, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says

items.title: Adaptive stress testing of autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions: A large language model (LLM) distillation approach
items.topic: Adaptive stress testing of autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions: A large language model (LLM) distillation approach
items.source: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
items.summary: Xiao Wen, Wentao Huang, Zhiyong Cui, and Sisi Jian from Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies used a large language model (LLM) to distill and adaptively test autonomous vehicle-pedestrian interactions. Their approach, published in January 2027, enhances the robustness of AV systems by simulating complex pedestrian behaviors, improving safety and reliability in real-world scenarios.

items.title: Accurate and sample efficient driver takeover time prediction in autonomous driving with privacy preservation: A federated meta attentive interpretable tabular learning approach
items.topic: Accurate and sample efficient driver takeover time prediction in autonomous driving with privacy preservation: A federated meta attentive interpretable tabular learning approach
items.source: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
items.summary: Weida Yang, Zhizhou Wu, Yinhai Wang, and Yunyi Liang from Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies developed a federated meta attentive interpretable tabular learning approach to predict driver takeover time accurately and efficiently while preserving privacy. Published in December 2026, their method improves the interpretability and efficiency of driver takeover predictions, crucial for enhancing the safety and trustworthiness of autonomous driving systems.

items.title: How do emotional cues influence drivers' pre-takeover readiness in automated driving? Evidence from olfaction-involved affective multimodal interaction
items.topic: How do emotional cues influence drivers' pre-takeover readiness in automated driving? Evidence from olfaction-involved affective multimodal interaction
items.source: Transportation Research Part F: Traffic Psychology and Behaviour
items.summary: Yinjie Lv, Chunhui Jing, Guanyu Lei, and Teng Zhao from Transportation Research Part F: Traffic Psychology and Behaviour investigated how emotional cues, particularly olfactory signals, influence drivers' pre-takeover readiness in automated driving. Their August 2026 study provides insights into the affective multimodal interactions that can enhance driver engagement and readiness, contributing to safer and more reliable human-vehicle interactions.
